questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The history of the city and the university. I wanted to be challenged academically, and get a perspective on the academic level and academic culture on one of the oldest universities in the world.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult to get any information about the course plan. It is not possible to obtain these informations through any platform, all information is given directly from the coordiateur pédagogique. I didn't hear from Sorbonne for a long time, so i was unsure of how the procedure was up to my stay.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did meet with my coordinateur before my courses started, and she offered to help with whatever questions i might have. I didn't have any specific questions, i was just doubted that i had inscribed everything correctly. She told me that everything was in order. Two months after we realised that i wasn't inscribed to Sorbonne correctly.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I found housing through af Facebook group for danes in Paris called 'Danskere i Paris'. In this group people are very helpfull. I was contacted by af danish/french guy, who was also going abroad. I rented his apartment, and have been very satisfied with the housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Find a place near campus, so the transportation isn't too difficult. The days are long at Sorbonne, so you easily hit rush-hour when commuting in the morning and evening.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Housing available for students is in Cité Universitaire. It's not anything Sorbonne can help you with. But the housing in Cité Universitaire is good and they are nice people.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There was an inscription day, but sadly i wasn't informed about this day proporly. I felt very lost for the first period at Sorbonne. The process of me getting a student card was very long and tiresome. I send multiple emails to the office for ERASMUS students, and finally it was clear that i wasn't inscribed properly. In the end everything came out well, but the process was very confusing and stressfull.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The office for ERASMUS students and my coordinateur pédagogique.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: The registration to classes was easy. Because the days at Sorbonne are so long, and each course has a lot of hours, the courses will easily overlap and therefore it is difficult to chose freely between courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be sure to get registration done before the courses start.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The courses are at a high academic level and the teachers are passionate about their work. The syllabus is big and a lot must be learned by heart, because none of the exams is with aids. It is great to be academically challenged, and i have respect for the academic culture at Sorbonne. I experienced multiple teachers, that were helpfull to foreigners, but also some teachers who couldn't take into account. the challenges an ERASMUS students faces, when joining a new university while learning a new language.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was high, considering that you should learn everything by heart, also long biochemical pathways and long scientific names. The concepts are not difficult to understand, but the amount of detail is difficult to manage. You study hard to be able to pass the exams, and afterwards you have learned a lot. As long as you can manage the stress, and also accept that it is not easy, especially when everything is in french.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is a lot more teaching at Sorbonne than at Copenhagen. You don't have any reading to do beforehand, and you wouldn't have the time to read beforehand. Also because many courses are 3 ECTS points courses, there is simply just more lectures and lessons than at Copenhagen. The understanding of the syllabus is through rote learning, where Copenhagen uses more analytical approaches, where the students form an understanding and then use it autonomously, in a slightly more free approach.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None, but everything in Paris is expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going to cafés and restaurants was more expensive than expected. Buying groceries was more expensive than expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I applied to join some clubs, but they were expensive and i didn't have the free time.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many activities were availible.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Meeting with french who want to learn danish, is a easy way to get a french friend, where a low level of french conversation is okay.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of concerts in Paris, and other cultural gatherings.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy. You get to know your local baker and your neighbour very easily. People are kind and welcoming.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The humor is very different from the danish humor.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and way of life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: That they need to reach out and ask for help a lot, and that it is their own responsibility to get their paperwork in order. They can expect, that they easily will be forgotten in the bureaucratic system.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Going to the exams and feeling accomplished that i took such a challenged, as studying biology in french, and completed it.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The language barrier.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
